name: RT-2 VLA Study Summary
observations: Source: "RT-2: Vision-Language-Action Models Transfer Web Knowledge to Robotic Control", Anthony Brohan et al., Google DeepMind, 2023 (arXiv 2307.15818v1), 26-page compressed PDF in pdf/embodied_ai_papers.

Core idea (VLA formulation): instead of bolting a VLM on as a high-level planner, co-fine-tune a web-scale VLM (PaLI-X 5B/55B, PaLM-E 12B) end-to-end so a single model maps camera images + text instruction -> low-level robot actions, with no new action-specific parameters or layers.

Key trick - actions as text tokens: 8-D action vector (6-DoF end-effector delta pos/rot, gripper extension, discrete terminate) is uniformly discretized into 256 bins per continuous dim and emitted as a space-separated token string, e.g. "terminate dposx dposy dposz drotx droty drotz gripper" -> "1 128 91 241 5 101 127"; 256 vocabulary slots are reserved for action tokens (PaLI-X maps to existing integer tokens; PaLM-E overwrites the 256 least-frequent tokens, a form of symbol tuning).

Training recipe: inputs formatted as VQA ("Q: what action should the robot take to [instruction]? A:"), outputs are action token strings; co-fine-tuning mixes original web VQA/captioning data with robot trajectories (upweighting the robot data in each batch) rather than fine-tuning on robot data alone - this preserves web concepts and measurably improves generalization vs. robot-only fine-tuning.

Inference engineering: restrict decoding to valid action tokens when prompted with a robot task (full vocabulary still allowed for normal VQA); serve large models from a multi-TPU cloud service queried over the network to hit real-time control rates (~1-3 Hz for 55B, ~5 Hz for 5B).

Results: ~6k real-world evaluation trials on a 7-DoF mobile manipulator; seen-task success on par with RT-1 (35M), but generalization to unseen objects/backgrounds/environments ~2x better than RT-1 and MOO and ~6x better than VC-1/R3M baselines; emergent skills (symbol understanding, reasoning/math/multilingual, person recognition) >3x average success over RT-1; 90% on simulated Language-Table with a PaLI-3B variant. Ablations: from-scratch training is far worse, co-fine-tuning > robot-only fine-tuning, and 55B > 5B for generalization.

Chain-of-thought variant: a few hundred gradient steps of PaLM-E on data augmented with an explicit "Plan:" sentence before the "Action:" tokens lets the model do multi-stage semantic reasoning (e.g., pick a rock as an improvised hammer, an energy drink for someone tired).

Stated limitations: no new physical skills from web data (skills limited to the robot-data distribution; web knowledge only re-purposes them), high inference cost for high-frequency control (motivating quantization/distillation), and few openly fine-tunable VLMs at the time.

Current best-practice tooling (LeRobot, /huggingface/lerobot v0.6.1, verified via Context7): pretrained VLA policies are loaded by checkpoint path rather than trained from scratch, e.g. `lerobot-train --policy.path=lerobot/xvla-base --policy.action_mode=auto --policy.max_action_dim=20` (auto action-dim padding/trimming, loss on real dims only) or a MolmoAct2 checkpoint with `--policy.action_mode=continuous --policy.chunk_size=10 --policy.n_action_steps=10 --policy.num_flow_timesteps=8` plus bf16/compile/gradient-checkpointing; ACT with `--policy.type=act --dataset.repo_id=...` remains the simple baseline. Adapter-style fine-tuning is supported via `--policy.freeze_qwen=true` (train action head only) or LoRA/FFT flags.

Best-practice deployment: for slow large VLAs (pi0, pi0.5, SmolVLA) use decoupled async inference - `python -m lerobot.async_inference.policy_server --host --port` on the GPU box plus `python -m lerobot.async_inference.robot_client --policy_type=smolvla --pretrained_name_or_path=lerobot/smolvla_base --actions_per_chunk=50 --chunk_size_threshold=0.5 --aggregate_fn_name=weighted_average`, tuning actions_per_chunk/chunk_size_threshold and enabling debug_visualize_queue_size. Alternatively `lerobot-rollout --inference.type=rtc --inference.rtc.execution_horizon=10 --inference.rtc.max_guidance_weight=10.0` (Real-Time Chunking) gives smooth motion despite latency, or `--strategy.type=sentry` for autonomous rollouts that auto-upload evaluation episodes to a dataset repo.

Practical takeaway for a similar workflow: start from an open pretrained VLA (LeRobot SmolVLA/X-VLA/pi0 checkpoints), keep the VLM backbone (LoRA or frozen-backbone adapter) rather than training from scratch, tokenize or chunk actions (chunk_size ~10-50 with overlapping-chunk aggregation), and serve inference asynchronously or with RTC so latency does not break closed-loop control.

name: RT-2: Vision-Language-Action Models (Brohan et al., 2023)
observations: Google DeepMind tech report, arXiv:2307.15818v1 [cs.RO], 28 Jul 2023; project page robotics-transformer2.github.io.

Introduces the vision-language-action (VLA) model category and the RT-2-PaLI-X (5B, 55B) and RT-2-PaLM-E (12B) instantiations, co-fine-tuned on web-scale VQA data plus RT-1 robot demonstration data (13 robots, 17 months, office kitchen).

name: LeRobot
observations: Hugging Face library for end-to-end robot learning; Context7 ID /huggingface/lerobot, version v0.6.1, Source Reputation High, benchmark score 70.54.

Provides lerobot-train / lerobot-rollout CLIs, ACT and diffusion imitation-learning baselines, and pretrained VLA policies (SmolVLA, pi0/pi0.5, X-VLA, MolmoAct2, VLA-JEPA) plus async policy-server/robot-client inference and Real-Time Chunking.
